specificFindings: Kenyon Otherwise and Carver are poems about ordinary routines, not experiments. The poet cherishes mundane life while recognising it could change.
Oliver Wild Geese permits imperfect virtue and despair as part of life; this is literary interpretation and does not endorse harming others or diagnose readers.
The research question moves from poem-derived factors to student diary reports. Typicality, routines, free time and new activities are recorded, not continuously observed minute by minute.
Associated with, most students reported, and predictors retain observational scope. Novelty is reported with all three wellbeing measures; no universal randomised causal result is invented.

Atypical days were richer without necessarily greater happiness; extra free time related to richness without greater meaning. Required work related to happiness and meaning, without an unsupported richness claim or overwork recommendation.
Vineyard, unfamiliar walk, baseball and an old-friend call illustrate departures from a particular persons routine; expensive travel or absolute worldwide novelty is not required.
The Fox and CNN comparison remains the authors hypothetical illustration: upset feelings can accompany interesting viewing. It is not a current network ranking or a statement about every viewer.
Study abroad ranking is conditional reasoning using novelty, complexity and perspective change, not a measured league table or guaranteed experience for every student.
Financial barriers are harder participation, not impossibility or lower ability. The Rotary award details and Haras recommendation concern this narrator, not universal available funding.
Hara recommends three Maine liberal arts colleges; liberal arts describes an educational institution rather than political ideology. His expectation about English learning remains an assumption.
Reese picks the narrator up at the airport and drives to Bates in Lewiston. Wagner in New York belongs to the preceding English-class phase.
The music question asks preference in music, not the later favourite-musician question. Dean Reese asks and the narrator answers Jazz. Neither character taste is inferred from race.

All14 inherited parent English/Chinese pairs were read from the compact source preview, preserving reported-study strength, quotations, conditional language, role attribution, chronology and full passage content.
Questions4,9,11,12,16 use full relevant parent context;21 includes preceding attribution context;23 and24 cite the original music question together with Dean Reese asked.
